# PLAN — ISSUE-288: Bound stalled coordinator Git network operations

Coordinator `fetch`, `push` and `ls-remote` can block forever. When a transport child (ssh, a
ControlPersist master, a proxy) still holds Git's output pipe, `CombinedOutput` keeps waiting for
EOF, even after the context has killed Git. This plan sends those three verbs through one bounded
runner in `internal/gitcredential`. The runner signals **only the Git leader it spawned and has not
yet reaped**. It never signals any transport child, closes its own pipe ends on a fixed budget, and
reports an interrupted push as an **unknown outcome**. Every push site keeps that outcome separate
from conflict, rejection and retry handling. Escaped-descendant cleanup and stronger process
boundaries are out of scope; they belong to draft 294.

Contract basis: this is the re-approved WorkUnit (bounded return, conservative cleanup). Earlier
plans promised to terminate descendants; this plan drops that. There is no sweep, no
process-group or numeric-group signal, no pidfd/ancestry targeting of children, and no
credential, auth or flag change. REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md is empty in this workspace, so the five
review revisions are resolved against the operator's list (see "Revision resolution").

## Dimensions
Set by the WorkUnit: size `multi_area`, uncertainty `known`, risk `sensitive`, profile `sensitive`.
No split needed. One new runner (~250 lines), one test-helper package, 14 small call-site edits
and focused tests fit well inside the 16h claim budget.

## What we know
- Every coordinator Git helper uses `exec.CommandContext` plus `CombinedOutput`/`Output` and has no
  network bound: `internal/coordination/store.go:165`, `internal/workspace/worktree.go:635-649`,
  `internal/gitcredential/environment.go:148`, `internal/fork/coordinator.go:703`,
  `internal/lease/checkpoint_reconcile.go:208`. `gitOutput` passes `context.Background()`
  (`worktree.go:636`), so the fetches at `worktree.go:124,295,392` and `recovery.go:51` have no bound at all.
- Go's `exec.Cmd.Wait` (GOROOT `os/exec/exec.go:922-960`) waits for the copy goroutines to reach
  EOF after the process exits. With `WaitDelay`, `ErrWaitDelay` is reported only when the exit was
  otherwise clean ("if err == nil"), so an `ExitError` hides the fact that I/O was still held. A
  runner built on exec's own goroutines therefore cannot tell "known failure, cleanup incomplete"
  apart from "known failure". That is why the plan uses caller-owned `*os.File` pipes.
- `gitcredential.Command` does not set `Setpgid`, and exec's default `Cancel` is
  `Process.Kill` on the leader only. Go 1.26 signals through the pidfd when one is available
  (GOROOT `os/pidfd_linux.go:126`). Either way, an unreaped child's pid cannot be recycled.
- The ten coordination push sites are `store.go:239, 333, 380, 632, 675`, `checkpoints.go:65`,
  `revoke.go:64, 102`, `cleanup.go:48` and `migration.go:102`. Several of them turn *any* push
  error into `ErrConflict` (`cleanup.go:49`, `migration.go:103`, `store.go:334-336` when expected is
  set) or into "no refs changed" (`migration.go:103`). Others re-read the ref and return
  `ErrConflict` when `actual != old` (`store.go:240-246`, `632-638`, `checkpoints.go:66-68`,
  `revoke.go:56-59`). For a push that was interrupted but **landed**, `actual == our commit`, so it
  is misreported as a conflict.
- `lease.Manager.mutate` retries on `ErrConflict` (`internal/lease/manager.go:1152-1172`). Today a
  landed-but-interrupted `CompareAndSwap` therefore re-applies the mutation on top of our own write,
  which is a blind republish. The fork loops `store.go:657-689` and `revoke.go:78-110` `continue` on
  index movement in the same way.
- `manager.go:2036` says "failed without changing either remote ref". That is false for an unknown outcome.
- Callers return publication errors without removing worktrees or branches
  (`workflow/execute_implementation.go:139-149`, `workflow/claim_budget.go:120-140`,
  `pr/service.go:1277-1283`), so the candidate is kept. This plan locks that in with tests.
- Retry already reinspects: `RecordCheckpoint` reloads state, fences on the recorded `HeadSHA`
  (`manager.go:1758-1858`) and pushes with exact `--force-with-lease` leases. `PublishPR` re-reads
  with `ls-remote` and requires `expectedHead` (`workspace/pr.go:522-529`).
- Precedent: `cmd.WaitDelay = time.Second` in `gitcredential/token.go:46` and in the sandbox runners.
- Tools available here: git 2.53.0, `/usr/bin/setsid`, `sh`, `sleep`, Go 1.26.10. These new
  files are absent at base: `internal/gitcredential/network.go`, `network_test.go`,
  `internal/testutil/gittransport/`, `changes/unreleased/288.md`, and the new `_test.go` files listed below.

## What we're assuming
- A1: a repo-local `core.sshCommand` plus `ssh.variant=simple` and an `ssh://fake.invalid/<abs>` URL
  drive coordinator Git through the fake transport even under `gitcredential.Configure`. It strips
  only `GIT_CONFIG_*`/`GIT_TRACE*`-class env vars and adds config through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, not
  `core.sshCommand`. Check: step 2's helper self-test runs `gitcredential.Output(..., "ls-remote", url)` in `Pass` mode.
- A2: the remote's `post-receive` hook runs after the ref update when receive-pack is started with
  `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` unset. The coordinator's `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` comes through env and would
  otherwise reach a local receive-pack. Check: the helper self-test asserts `Landed()` and that the remote ref moved.
- A3: `os.Pipe` read ends on Linux are pollable, so `Close` unblocks a pending `Read`. Check: the
  `TestNetworkClosesHeldPipesWithinBudget` reader-exit assertion.
- A4: the 10-minute default network bound does not cut off legitimate coordinator fetches. These
  fetch pinned SHAs or refs, not full clones. It is not user-configurable (no new flags). The
  cheapest check is that existing suites pass unchanged.

## Open questions
- Real OpenSSH ControlMaster/ControlPersist behaviour is not exercised here (no sshd in the
  sandbox). The fake detached holder (step 2) models the documented stderr-holding master. Real-ssh
  verification is a manual follow-up and does not block implementation.
- Leader stuck in uninterruptible sleep (D state) cannot be produced on purpose. It is covered
  through the `waitLeader` seam (step 1); the real kernel case is documented, not reproduced.

## Revision resolution (operator list → plan element)
1. Bounded leader cancellation and owned I/O → step 1: kill the leader, `reapGrace`, `ioGrace`, close our read ends.
2. Shared or ambiguous **direct** children are protected; no killing heuristic → every transport
   child counts as ambiguous. Only the unreaped leader is signaled. Sweep/child targeting is
   deleted from the design, not added.
3. Immutable results, broadcast completion, every setup/error path, honest syscall limits → step 1 "Run record" and "Limits".
4. Self-contained tests, both workspace callers, all ten push sites, landed-push retry and
   authoritative-successor tests, candidate retention → TEST_PLAN T1–T24.
5. No credential/auth changes, no numeric-group signaling, strict unknown-vs-known → steps 1, 3 and 4; T8/T9/T13.

## Design

### Step 1 — `internal/gitcredential/network.go` (new)
Exported surface (minimal):
- `var ErrInterrupted = errors.New("git network operation interrupted before Git reported a result")`
- `var ErrCleanupIncomplete = errors.New("git process cleanup incomplete")`
- `func IsNetwork(args []string) bool`: true when `args[0]` is `fetch`, `push` or `ls-remote`.
- `func Network(ctx context.Context, root string, combined bool, args ...string) ([]byte, error)`.
  `combined` gives `CombinedOutput` semantics (one pipe for stdout and stderr). Otherwise stdout is
  returned and stderr is captured on its own pipe into `ExitError.Stderr`, as `cmd.Output()` does.
  The output is raw; callers keep redacting it as they do today.

Unexported budgets and seams (tests in the package override them):
`networkTimeout = 10*time.Minute`, `reapGrace = 5*time.Second`, `ioGrace = 2*time.Second`,
`cleanupReports io.Writer = os.Stderr`, `newPipe = os.Pipe`, `waitLeader = (*exec.Cmd).Wait`.

Sequence:
1. `bctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, networkTimeout)`. An earlier caller deadline wins.
   `defer cancel()`.
2. **Setup paths.** None of these start a process or a worker, and all opened files are closed:
   - (a) `ctx.Err() != nil` → return `fmt.Errorf("git %s not started: %w", op, ctx.Err())`. This is
     **not** `ErrInterrupted`; nothing was sent.
   - (b) `Command(bctx, root, args...)` error (token, config) → return it unchanged.
   - (c) the first or second `newPipe` fails → close every end already opened, then return.
   - (d) `cmd.Start` fails → close all four ends and return a redacted, wrapped start error. Not `ErrInterrupted`.
   - `cmd.Stdin` stays nil (`/dev/null`). Network verbs never take input; the coordination `run`
     with non-empty input on a network verb returns an error.
3. After `Start`, close our copies of the write ends at once. Children hold the only write ends.
4. Workers: one reader goroutine per read end copies into a `bytes.Buffer` (unbounded, as today;
   `ls-remote` output is parsed) and closes `readDone[i]` when it finishes. One waiter goroutine runs
   `waitLeader(cmd)`, stores `ProcessState`/err in the record and closes `reaped`. exec's own ctx
   watcher calls `Process.Kill` (leader only) when `bctx` is done.
5. Orchestration: wait for `reaped`, or for `bctx.Done()` followed by at most `reapGrace` for
   `reaped`. Then start an `ioGrace` timer and wait for every `readDone`. On timeout, `Close` each
   read end (this unblocks the readers, per A3), wait for the readers to exit, and mark
   `ioHeld = true`. Read ends are closed on every path before `Network` returns, so the parent
   never keeps a descriptor.
6. Classification. The record is written once and never mutated after it is returned:
   - **Known result**: the leader was reaped and `WaitStatus.Exited()`. Exit 0 → `(out, nil)`. If
     `ioHeld`, also write one redacted line to `cleanupReports`: "swarm: warning: git <op>
     completed, but a process that inherited its output was still running after 2s; it was left
     running because SwarmOS cannot prove it exclusively owns it (for example a shared SSH master)".
     A known success never becomes an error: that would turn a landed push into a "failure".
     Non-zero exit → the `*exec.ExitError` itself. If `ioHeld`, return a `runError` that wraps both
     the `ExitError` and `ErrCleanupIncomplete`. A known rejection still classifies as rejection.
   - **Interrupted**: the leader was killed by a signal (by us or anyone else), or was not reaped
     within `reapGrace`. Return a `runError` wrapping `ErrInterrupted` and the cause
     (`bctx.Err()`: `DeadlineExceeded` or the parent's `Canceled`; if `bctx` is not done, the
     `ExitError`), plus `ErrCleanupIncomplete` when `ioHeld` or the leader is unreaped.
   - `runError{msg string; errs []error}` has `Unwrap() []error`. Its message is built through
     `redact` and carries operation-specific guidance:
     - push: "remote outcome unknown: the push may have landed. Rerun the same swarm command; it
       re-reads the remote and authoritative state before publishing. Do not force-push; the local
       candidate commit is kept."
     - fetch: "no remote refs were changed; rerun when the remote is reachable."
     - ls-remote: "the remote head was not observed; rerun when the remote is reachable."
     - Cleanup suffixes: "Git (pid N) did not exit within 5s of SIGKILL" or "a process that
       inherited Git's output was left running; SwarmOS signals only the Git process it started".
7. **Run record and broadcast.** The unexported `networkRun` holds `reaped`, `readDone[]` and
   `settled` channels. `settled` is closed by a closer goroutine after the waiter and every reader
   finish. A late waiter (unreaped leader) only writes into the record's own fields before closing
   its channel. It never touches the returned error, buffers or files. Tests observe it through an
   unexported `lastRun` hook.
8. **Limits (documented in the doc comment).** The return is bounded by roughly
   `min(deadline, 10m) + reapGrace + ioGrace`. These parts are *not* bounded:
   - `cmd.Start` (fork/exec) is synchronous.
   - `GitHubToken` inside `Command` has its own bound (`token.go:46`).
   - A waiter blocked in `wait4` on a D-state leader sits on an OS thread that cannot be
     interrupted. It is leaked until the kernel reaps the leader, and that is reported as cleanup incomplete.
   - `Kill` is a single syscall. Pipe reads go through the netpoller and are interrupted by `Close`.
   - Surviving transport children may keep remote connections open, which is exactly why a push is reported as unknown.

`Output` (`environment.go:148`) dispatches to `Network(ctx, root, false, args...)` when
`IsNetwork(args)`. The wrapping stays the same: `fmt.Errorf("git %s: %w", redact(args), err)`.
This covers `lease/cleanup_preview.go:150`, `lease/cleanup.go:121,191`,
`pr/service.go:1242`, `cli/submit_freshness.go:39` and `harness/scaffold.go:159`.

### Step 2 — `internal/testutil/gittransport` (new, test-only helper package)
`New(t, bare string) *Transport` writes these files into `t.TempDir()`:
- An `ssh` script. It records `$$` in `clients`, reads the per-service mode file (`upload`,
  `receive`), parses `git-upload-pack '/p'` / `git-receive-pack '/p'` from `$2`, and runs one of:
  - `pass`: `exec env -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT git <svc> "$p"`
  - `hang`: poll for the `release` file every 50 ms, holding stdio
  - `reject`: print a fixed message to stderr and `exit 128`
  - `land-hang`: like `pass`, but the bare repo's `post-receive` hook writes `landed` and polls for `release`
  - `holder`: start `setsid sh -c '<poll release>' </dev/null >/dev/null &` with stderr inherited,
    record its pid in `master`, then `pass`
- A `post-receive` hook in `bare`.

Methods: `Configure(t, repo, remote)` sets `core.sshCommand`, `ssh.variant=simple` and the
`ssh://fake.invalid<bare>` URL. Also `Set(service, mode)`, `Clients() []int`, `Master() int`,
`Landed() bool`, `Release()` and `Alive(pid) bool` (`kill(pid,0)==nil` and `/proc/<pid>/stat`
state not `Z`). `t.Cleanup` calls `Release` and then requires every recorded pid to be dead within
10 s, which also verifies that no fixture process leaks.

### Step 3 — route coordinator helpers (both workspace helpers included)
- `coordination/store.go:165` `run`: if `gitcredential.IsNetwork(args)`, return an error when input
  is non-empty, otherwise call `Network(ctx, s.root, true, args...)`. Keep the same message format and redaction.
- `workspace/worktree.go:639` `gitOutputContext`, and through it `gitOutput` at `:635`: use the
  same dispatch. This covers both workspace push callers (`PushForkCheckpointFrom` `:239` and
  `PublishPR` `pr.go:529`) and every workspace fetch/ls-remote.
- `fork/coordinator.go:703` `runGitWithToken` and `lease/checkpoint_reconcile.go:208` `checkpointGit`: same dispatch.

### Step 4 — coordination push sites (all ten)
- Add `var ErrPublicationUnknown = errors.New("coordination publication outcome unknown; reload authoritative state before any retry")` in `store.go`.
- Add `func (s *GitStore) push(ctx context.Context, args ...string) error`. It calls `s.run`; when
  `errors.Is(err, gitcredential.ErrInterrupted)` it returns
  `fmt.Errorf("%w: %w", ErrPublicationUnknown, err)`. It never wraps `ErrConflict`.
- At each site, replace `s.run(ctx, "", push...)` (or `s.git.run`) with `s.push`, then add
  `if errors.Is(err, ErrPublicationUnknown) { return "", err }` (`nil, err` for migration). This
  check comes **before** any re-read, `ErrConflict` mapping, "no refs changed" message or loop
  `continue`. Sites: `store.go:239, 333, 380, 632, 675`; `checkpoints.go:65`; `revoke.go:64, 102`;
  `cleanup.go:48`; `migration.go:102`. Known rejections keep today's mapping, byte for byte.
- `lease/manager.go:2036`: on `errors.Is(err, coordination.ErrPublicationUnknown)`, return
  `fmt.Errorf("atomic PR publication outcome unknown; rerun swarm pr submit %d, which reloads issue state and the PR head before publishing: %w", number, err)`.
  Keep the existing message otherwise. No other lease logic changes: `mutate` already retries
  only on `ErrConflict`, and `manager.go:1857` maps only `ErrConflict`.

### Step 5 — changelog and lessons
- `changes/unreleased/288.md`, one bullet: "Bound coordinator Git fetch, push and ls-remote so
  stalled transports return with retry guidance; interrupted pushes are reported as an unknown
  outcome and never retried blindly."
- `.swarm/active/LESSONS.md` (already written by the planner).

## HANDOFF
**Entry points**
- `internal/gitcredential/environment.go:148` (`Output` dispatch)
- new `internal/gitcredential/network.go`
- `internal/coordination/store.go:165` (`run`) and the push sites at `store.go:239, 333, 380, 632, 675`, `checkpoints.go:65`, `revoke.go:64, 102`, `cleanup.go:48`, `migration.go:102`
- `internal/workspace/worktree.go:635-649`
- `internal/fork/coordinator.go:703`
- `internal/lease/checkpoint_reconcile.go:208`
- `internal/lease/manager.go:2036`

**Tests and fixtures to extend.** Reuse the setups in these tests; switch the remote to
`gittransport` just before the operation under test:
- coordination: `newRetentionFixture` (`checkpoints_test.go:19`), `newRevokeFixture`
  (`revoke_test.go:24`), the ledger fixture with `seedBranchLedger` (`migration_test.go:24`),
  `TestCleanupAtomicBranchAndStateFences` (`cleanup_test.go:12`),
  `TestForkIndexedStoreAtomicCapAndReplay` (`store_test.go:186`),
  `TestPRPublishRequiresCapturedStateAndRemoteHead` (`store_test.go:99`)
- `TestDroppedCheckpointPublicationFence` (`lease/recovery_publication_test.go:18`)
- `TestPRPublishExactHeadLeaseAndPreservesPrimaryCheckout` (`workspace/pr_test.go:102`)
- `TestPushForkCheckpointFromAllowsOriginOnlyWhenNotUpstream` (`workspace/upstream_remote_test.go:107`)

**Focused commands**
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/gitcredential/... ./internal/testutil/gittransport/...`
- `go test -race -count=1 -run 'Network|Interrupted|Landed|Successor' ./internal/coordination/... ./internal/workspace/... ./internal/lease/... ./internal/fork/...`
- then `make check`

**Assumptions already checked**
- Go's `ErrWaitDelay` masking: read in GOROOT `os/exec/exec.go`.
- pidfd signaling: GOROOT `os/pidfd_linux.go`.
- No `Setpgid` on coordinator Git: `grep -rn Setpgid internal` shows only `process/tree_unix.go`, which coordinator Git does not use.
- No test asserts the push error messages being changed: grep of each message string under `internal`, `cmd` and `docs` returned none.
- The new files are absent: checked with `ls`.

**Reopen the plan instead of widening the change if:**
- A1 or A2 fails and the fake transport needs env or credential changes in `Configure`.
- Any site needs in-process reinspection or retry to pass.
- A test seems to require signaling a transport child.
- `networkTimeout` breaks an existing suite.
- Non-network Git verbs appear to need the runner.

**What this change breaks** (from greps)
- The push error text for *interrupted* pushes changes at the 10 sites. No test asserts these strings.
- `manager.go:2036` text changes only for the unknown outcome.
- Known-rejection messages and `ErrConflict` mapping are unchanged, including `migration_test.go:230`,
  `revoke_test.go:238`, `cleanup_test.go:12` and `store_test.go:16, 99`.
- `TestConcurrentIssueReadsStayPinnedAndTransportErrorsSurface` (`store_test.go:150`) is unchanged:
  ordinary transport errors stay known failures.
- `docs/fork-mode.md:61` (client timeout re-query) is unaffected and preserved unchanged.
- No CLI flags or docs are added.
- Error values that used to be a bare `*exec.ExitError` stay matchable with `errors.As`.

**Recommended follow-ups (not in this WorkUnit)**
- `PushForkCheckpointFrom` leases on a freshly observed fork head (`worktree.go:226-239`), so a
  retry can replace another writer on that claim-scoped fork branch. Consider fencing it on the
  recorded head.
- Real OpenSSH ControlMaster verification.
- Stronger process boundary (draft 294).

## Operator guidance

> The operator approved bounded return and conservative safe cleanup; the WorkUnit has been edited/reapproved to match. Stronger boundary design is separate draft294. Resolve all five latest REVIEW revisions against this NEW contract, do not carry obsolete descendant-termination promises. Treat shared/ambiguous DIRECT children as protected too: ancestry/pidfd is not exclusive-use proof. It is valid to conservatively classify all externally configured transports as ambiguous and report incomplete cleanup rather than invent a killing heuristic. Prefer deleting unsafe sweep/child-targeting complexity. Git leader cancellation and owned I/O must be bounded; any child actually signaled needs independent exclusive-use proof and verified exit, otherwise do not signal. Define immutable results plus broadcast completion for all late workers, every setup/error path and accurate synchronous-syscall limits. Restore self-contained test definitions, both workspace callers and all ten coordination push sites, explicit landed-push retry/authoritative successor tests and candidate retention. Retain no credential/auth changes, no numeric-group signaling and strict unknown-vs-known outcome distinction. Implementable narrow plan only; no new dependencies or boundary work.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->

# TEST_PLAN — ISSUE-288

Every test is self-contained. It builds its own temporary bare remote and clone with `gitfixture`,
drives coordinator Git through `internal/testutil/gittransport` (PLAN step 2), and releases its own
fixture processes; `gittransport`'s `t.Cleanup` verifies they are dead.

**Old-behaviour proof.** Each hang test runs the call under test in a goroutine with a
**watchdog of 45 s**, which is far above the bound. On timeout the test fails with
"did not return within 45s (unbounded Git wait)", then calls `Release()` so the goroutine unwinds.
The hang is held by the fixture's `release` file, not by timing, so on the base revision every hang
test fails deterministically at runtime. On the fixed code the bound assertion is
`elapsed < deadline + reapGrace + ioGrace + 3s`.

Cross-package tests use a caller context deadline of 5 s. They cannot shrink the unexported
budgets, so their bound is 5 + 5 + 2 + 3 = 15 s. In-package `gitcredential` tests set
`networkTimeout = 300ms`, `reapGrace = 1s` and `ioGrace = 300ms`.

**Shorthand used below**
- **"Classified interrupted"** means:
  - `errors.Is(err, gitcredential.ErrInterrupted)` is true;
  - `errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` is true, or `context.Canceled` where stated;
  - the error message contains the operation-specific guidance from PLAN step 1.6;
  - the error message contains no token, `basic `, or absolute temp path.
- **"Survivors"** means:
  - every pid in `Clients()` and `Master()` is still `Alive` right after the call returns, so they were never signaled;
  - a test-started unrelated `sleep 60` (via `exec.Command`, in the test's own process group) is `Alive`;
  - the test kills that `sleep` itself in cleanup.

## Acceptance criterion 1
> Hanging-transport regressions fail against the old behaviour and show bounded return, effective cancellation, a retained candidate and safe operation-specific retry guidance. Git and owned I/O stop within the budget, and unresolved child cleanup is reported explicitly. Shared direct or detached SSH masters, concurrent clients and unrelated processes survive. Any child that is signaled has independent proof of exclusive ownership and a verified exit.

All tests in this group are in `internal/gitcredential/network_test.go` (new) unless a file is named.

| ID | Test | Setup → action | Assertions |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | `TestNetworkBoundsHangingTransport/{fetch,push,ls-remote}` | `upload` or `receive` = `hang`; `Network(ctx, clone, true, <verb>…)` | Bounded return (watchdog proves the old hang). Classified interrupted with `DeadlineExceeded`. Error wraps `ErrCleanupIncomplete` and says the inheriting process was left running. The guidance text differs per verb (push: "outcome unknown… Do not force-push"; fetch: "no remote refs were changed"; ls-remote: "remote head was not observed"). |
| T2 | `TestNetworkCancellationReapsOnlyTheLeader` | `hang`; capture the leader through the `lastRun` hook | The leader's `ProcessState` is non-nil, `Signaled()`, signal `SIGKILL`. `syscall.Wait4(pid, WNOHANG)` returns `ECHILD`, so the leader exit is verified. Survivors (the direct transport child is shared/ambiguous and was **not** signaled). The leader is the only signaled process: it was started by this runner and unreaped, so its pid cannot be recycled. That is the exclusive-ownership proof. |
| T3 | `TestNetworkParentCancelIsInterruptedCanceled` | `hang`; cancel the parent context after the fixture records a client | Classified interrupted with `context.Canceled`, not `DeadlineExceeded`. Bounded. |
| T4 | `TestNetworkDetachedMasterKnownSuccess` | `upload` = `holder`; `ls-remote` | Returns `(out, nil)` with the correct ref line, so the known success is kept. `cleanupReports` (a test buffer) holds one warning line without a path or token. `Master()` is alive (detached master survives). The call returns within `ioGrace + 3s` while the master still holds stderr. |
| T5 | `TestNetworkDetachedMasterKnownFailure` | `holder`, then `fetch` of a nonexistent SHA | `errors.As(err, *exec.ExitError)` and `errors.Is(err, ErrCleanupIncomplete)`. `!errors.Is(err, ErrInterrupted)`, so a known failure stays distinct from an unknown outcome. Master is alive. |
| T6 | `TestNetworkSharedDirectClientAndConcurrentClient` | Client A: `upload` = `hang` with a short deadline. Concurrently, client B runs `ls-remote` through a second clone whose transport is in `pass` mode (separate `Transport`) with a longer deadline, plus an independent `git ls-remote` started by the test through `gitfixture`. | A is interrupted. B and the fixture client both succeed. A's direct transport child (`Clients()[0]`, treated as possibly shared) is alive. Unrelated `sleep` is alive. |
| T7 | `TestNetworkClosesHeldPipesWithinBudget` | `hang`; the `newPipe` seam records every `*os.File` | After return, each recorded file's `Fd()` returns `^uintptr(0)` (closed). The `readDone` channels are closed. `settled` closes within 1 s once the leader is reaped. Run non-parallel; `/proc/self/fd` count after `settled` equals the count before. |
| T8 | `TestNetworkUnreapedLeaderIsLateWorker` | `waitLeader` seam blocks until the test releases it, then calls `cmd.Wait`; `hang` | Return is bounded at `deadline + reapGrace + ioGrace + slack`. The error wraps `ErrInterrupted` and `ErrCleanupIncomplete` and its message says "did not exit within". The read ends are already closed. `settled` is still open.
